header:
Date: 2027-04-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Sanjay Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood Solutions); Tom Delgado (Aegis Head of ML), Priya Kapoor (Aegis Product), Ethan Morales (Aegis Infra), Leah Ortiz (Aegis Data Ops)
summary: POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan and load/benchmark sizing. Customer wants a two-week pilot to validate hallucination rates, structured-output conformance, and latency at target concurrency. Action items agreed for data samples, benchmark config, and security/pricing paperwork.
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're gonna run about an hour. Quick intros?
[00:12] Tom (Aegis): Tom here, Head of ML at Aegis, Priya and Ethan with me.
[00:18] Priya (Aegis): Hi all.
[00:20] Jamie: Great. The agenda is to align on what counts as success for the POC, what load you'll run, and how we'll score quality — specifically golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, and timelines. Sanjay will dig into the benchmark config.
[00:34] Sanjay (Redwood SE): Yeah I'll be focused on the bench plan. Can you share upfront what your top success criteria look like?
[00:42] Tom: Two big things — first we need hallucination under control, that's the blocker for product shipping. Second is latency: our UX team needs p95 under ~350ms for single-turn Q&A. Also throughput matters for peak sale windows.
[00:59] Priya: And for quality we need consistent structured output — JSON with specific keys. If the model returns free text we fail validation.
[01:08] Maya (Redwood Solutions): Good callout. We'll include format checks in the eval harness.
[01:12] Ethan: On infra constraints: we're in AWS us-east-1, we require VPC peering for Private deployment evaluation, KMS-managed keys for any persisted caches, and we have strict egress rules.
[01:26] Jamie: Noted. We support both Hosted and Dedicated during the POC; Dedicated gives you the predictable p95 but takes a bit more setup. Which is preferred for this pilot?
[01:36] Tom: We'd prefer Hosted first to move fast, but if latency doesn't meet the bar we'll consider Dedicated.
[01:42] Sanjay: Okay. For the golden prompts, how many anchor cases do you want? In our experience 200–500 items for golden set is typical to surface regressions.
[01:53] Priya: We can start with 300 golden prompts that represent high-value intents — a mix of short and long prompts for receipts, return flows, and product lookup.
[02:03] Sanjay: Great. For regression tests we'll set up a golden set (300) plus a regression run of 1,000 anonymized queries sampled from production each week during the pilot. Regression will include precision checks for entity extraction and schema conformance.
[02:17] Tom: Sounds good. On hallucination checks what metric do you use? False assertion rate?
[02:22] Sanjay: We typically use a combination: a binary hallucination flag per response (did it invent facts about product IDs, pricing, or policies) plus a severity score (0-3) if it contradicts provided context. We'll set an alert if overall false assertion rate exceeds 2% on the golden set.
[02:39] Leah (Aegis): Who'll label hallucinations — do you want us to do initial human labeling?
[02:44] Maya: Ideally yes — you label 200 of the golden prompts for ground truth, Redwood will run automated scoring and then we can sample for adjudication.
[02:54] Priya: Budget for labeling is tight, we can commit to labeling 200 and Redwood can handle the rest.
[02:59] Sanjay: That works. For scoring approach: we'll compute multiple metrics per example — format pass/fail, schema field F1 (for extracted fields), hallucination flag, and a composite score that weights format heavily for acceptance. Composite threshold for go/no-go we'll set at 0.92 on the golden set initially.
[03:20] Tom: Composite 0.92 OK but we might negotiate based on user testing.
[03:24] Jamie: On load sizing, Ethan can you describe peak qps and token distributions?
[03:29] Ethan: Peak concurrent sessions hit ~600 users in a 5-minute flash sale, average qps during peak 90 qps, but most requests are short — median 60 tokens each, 95th 400 tokens.
[03:43] Sanjay: For pilot benchmarking we'll run staged load: baseline 10 qps, ramp to 100 qps sustained for 15 minutes, then spike tests up to 200 qps for short bursts. We'll capture p50/p90/p95/p99 latency and GPU utilization.
[03:56] Jamie: Do you have a SLB or LB fronting the service? Any rate limit patterns?
[04:00] Ethan: We use an internal edge with a token bucket limiter. We'll give you the config.
[04:06] Priya: One more on cost — if we use Hosted for pilot how do you estimate cost for our 2-week run?
[04:12] Jamie: I'll send a cost estimate with two scenarios: conservative (no batching) and optimized (with batching and KV cache enabled). Expect the optimized scenario to reduce per-token cost 30–40% depending on cache hit rates.
[04:24] Tom: For benchmarks we also want to validate kv-cache benefits for our session flows — we have many multi-turn sessions.
[04:30] Sanjay: We'll include a multi-turn workload with KV cache enabled/disabled comparisons and report token savings.
[04:36] Leah: Regarding data residency and logs — we cannot ship PII outside our VPC. Is there a way to run the pilot with minimal retention?
[04:44] Jamie: Yes, Redwood can disable retention and redact tokens; we can also run Private deployment in your VPC for an on-prem like setup for later stages. For the pilot, Hosted with retention off should suffice to validate quality.
[04:58] Priya: What's the expected timeline to run the pilot once we sign off?
[05:02] Jamie: Setup typically 3–5 business days for a Hosted pilot (credentialing, tokens, minimal network setup). Dedicated or Private takes longer — ~2 weeks. So if we get samples by 4/13 we can start the pilot week of 4/20.
[05:15] Tom: That aligns. For acceptance gates — recap what passes looks like?
[05:20] Sanjay: Pass criteria: composite score >= 0.92 on golden set; hallucination rate <= 2% on golden set; format schema pass-rate >= 98%; p95 latency <= 350ms on peak-simulated load for Hosted (if not met then discuss Dedicated).
[05:36] Priya: Also want automated regression not to degrade by more than 1.5% week over week.
[05:41] Sanjay: We'll add weekly regression runs during the pilot and baseline at pilot start.
[05:45] Tom: Any recommended size for regression sets beyond the 1,000 sample?
[05:50] Sanjay: 1k weekly should be fine; for daily smoke tests we'll run 100 random samples.
[05:55] Jamie: On reporting — we'll deliver a benchmark report with latency, cost per token, hallucination summary, and a golden-set scorecard. We'll also include a runbook for Dedicated if you want to move forward.
[06:07] Leah: Do you have an internal eval UI we can use to inspect failures?
[06:11] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console has a per-example inspector for golden set failures and hallucination flags; we'll give you access.
[06:18] Tom: Security wise we need SOC2 docs and an audit log of requests.
[06:22] Jamie: We'll attach SOC2 report and a data access/Audit Log extract sample. Also, we support SAML SSO and RBAC for the console.
[06:33] Priya: OK, sounds like we have a plan. Quick clarifying Q: For composite scoring weight — what's the weight on format vs entity F1 vs hallucination?
[06:40] Sanjay: Proposed: format pass (50%), entity F1 (30%), hallucination penalty (20% inverted so hallucination lowers the score). We can tweak per case.
[06:50] Tom: Fine. Any blockers for the setup?
[06:54] Ethan: We'll need the VPC peering doc and an IP allowlist. Also we need to confirm KMS integration for any persisted caches.
[07:03] Jamie: I'll send the networking checklist and the KMS integration guide in the next email.
[07:08] Priya: Great.
[07:10] Jamie: Let's recap next steps: Jamie sends pricing and security docs; Sanjay sends benchmark plan and schedule; Aegis shares sample queries and golden prompts (200 labeled, 100 unlabeled).
[07:22] Tom: We'll aim to get samples to you by 4/13.
[07:27] Jamie: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the kickoff.
[07:33] End of meeting.

Notes: Transcription contains occasional speaker label mismatches and minor misspellings from auto-transcript (e.g., "kv cache" as "K V cache"), timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts referenced: pilot-bench-config.xlsx (Google Drive), POC-security-checklist.pdf (link provided by Jamie), Redwood Console access request form.
notes: Pilot duration proposed: 2 weeks. Golden set: 300 anchor prompts (200 labeled by customer). Regression weekly: 1,000 samples. Acceptance gates: composite >= 0.92, hallucinations <= 2%, schema pass >= 98%, p95 latency <= 350ms. Hosted start with option to move to Dedicated if latency fails.
